name: Render
description: Rendering the structured specification into documents a person reads.

text: A document carries what the specification means, not what the tool
needs in order to find things. The words a glossary rejects stay out,
because they record where a project drifted rather than what its
vocabulary is, and a reader is handed one at the line it was tripped on
instead. The `include` globs stay out for the same reason, and a
contract's marker with them: they say where to look and what to look
Notes are the other half of that sentence. They are what a
specification means and nothing the tool finds things by, so they are
rendered whole — and they are a document rather than a reference line,
which is what lets a worked example live in one and be compared against
A document is derived, so a run replaces what the last one wrote. What
`init` refuses to overwrite is a reference line, and this is not one.
An absent specification is nothing to render rather than a comparison
that could not be made, so it is passed over in silence. Render records
where Verify certifies, and the run that would otherwise pass an absent
reference line off as agreement is `verify`, which still stops.

scenarios.title: The vocabulary becomes a document
scenarios.then: a glossary document is written under the configured documents path

scenarios.title: One document per feature
given: a behavior specification holding one file per feature
scenarios.then: each feature is written to a document named after the file declaring it

scenarios.title: A specification the configuration switched off
given: a .sumi.json declaring the glossary is not to be rendered
scenarios.then: the switched-off specification leaves no document behind

scenarios.title: Nothing to render is not a failure
A second run brings the document up to date
given: a project whose rendered document no longer matches the specification
scenarios.then: the document is replaced by what the specification now says

scenarios.title: A specification that could not be read
given: a behavior specification that is not readable JSON
scenarios.then: the file is named as one that could not be read

scenarios.title: One document per kind of contract
scenarios.then: each definition is written to a document named after the file registering it

scenarios.title: An interface the project keeps but does not publish
given: a definition registering one internal interface and one that is not
scenarios.then: the page carries only the one that is not internal

scenarios.title: A kind with nothing to publish
given: a definition whose every interface is internal
scenarios.then: no page is written for it

scenarios.title: The shape an interface is reached by
given: a contract registering the parameters of one interface and none of another
scenarios.then: the one carries its shape beside its name and the other is named alone
